**Group:** Dinoflagellates  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A thecate dinoflagellate that is strongly compressed laterally, so it looks like two watch-glasses joined edge to edge (clamshell). The anterior end bears a funnel-shaped cingular list (collar), and prominent wing (or sail) sulcal lists project from the left ventral margin. Often filled with food vaccole. Key features: lateral flattening, sail-like sulcal lists.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **ceratium** | Ceratium has long apical and antapical horns; Dinophysis has no horns but conspicuous cingular and sulcal lists. |
| **prorocentrum** | Prorocentrum splits into two flat valves along a sagittal suture with an apical spine; Dinophysis has the funnel collar and sail lists. |
